assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Time window assumed to be 1-10 September 2026, compared with 22-31 August 2026 as the baseline.
Metric assumed to be attempt_success_rate for UPI.
caveats: The data-quality scan found no issues for 1-10 Sep (duplicates, missing values, orphan keys, timestamps, ingestion lag, volume).
Hourly and daily views shown are partial extracts of the underlying tables, so some days and hours are not displayed here.

facts.text: UPI attempt success rate was 92.1% in 1-10 Sep (58,146 successes out of 63,131 attempts), versus 93.0% in 22-31 Aug (60,069 out of 64,606). It fell 0.87pp, and the difference is statistically significant (p-value 2.78e-09) and practically significant.
The 95% confidence intervals do not overlap: 92.78%-93.17% for the baseline and 91.89%-92.31% for early September.
Across 22 Aug-10 Sep the median daily success rate was 92.51%. The lowest day was 2 Sep at 91.77% and the highest was 26 Aug at 93.42%. No anomaly windows were flagged in the daily series.
Among the daily rates shown, 1 Sep (92.6%) and 2 Sep (91.77%) were below every baseline day except 25 Aug (92.24%).
The segment scan ranks issuer as the dimension that most concentrates the change. Zephyr's success rate fell from 93.42% to 89.59%.
For Zephyr, hours 19, 20, 21 and 22 show statistically significant drops. The worst is hour 19, which fell 11.92pp. Other hours shown (0-11) show no significant change.
For Zephyr, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts (745 failures in the current window versus 53 in the baseline). This is the largest shift among Zephyr failure codes.

Across all UPI, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT rose from 0.29 to 1.39 per 100 attempts (879 failures versus 189), the largest rise of any failure code. UPI_COLLECT_EXPIRED edged down from 2.50 to 2.35 per 100 attempts.
Other segments (acquirer, region, merchant group, category, channel) show much weaker concentration than issuer.

response.headline: UPI attempt success rate fell 0.87pp, from 93.0% (22-31 Aug) to 92.1% in 1-10 Sep. The drop is statistically significant and is concentrated in one issuer, Zephyr, where a spike in UPI PSP timeouts stands out.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the PSP/issuer incident logs for Zephyr in the evenings of 1-10 Sep, review the hour x date view to see when the timeouts began, and compare timeout rates by PSP route.
hypotheses.rationale: Zephyr's rate fell sharply, its drops are significant only in hours 19-22, and UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts rose about 14-fold for Zephyr and about 5-fold across UPI, while other failure codes barely moved.
hypotheses.text: A PSP-side timeout problem affecting Zephyr UPI transactions, mainly in the evening hours (19:00-22:59), is the main driver of the overall dip.

recommendations.rationale: The timeout spike is the clearest failure-code shift and is concentrated in one issuer and a few hours.
recommendations.text: Escalate to the PSP and Zephyr with the hour-by-date timeout evidence, focusing on 19:00-22:59.
